topic.topicDisplayName: AA Amyloidosis secondary to chronic arthritis
topic.coverageNote: Open review of systemic AA amyloidosis. It names rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, and chronic juvenile arthritis among the inflammatory causes, and it gives the precursor protein, the Congo-red standard, SAP scintigraphy, and the proteinuria presentation.

mcqs.question: What is the main protein in AA amyloid deposits, and which cytokines drive its hepatic production?

options.A: Serum amyloid A, produced in response to IL-1, IL-6, and TNF
options.B: Immunoglobulin light chain, produced in response to IL-17 only
options.C: Transthyretin, produced in response to IL-6 only
options.D: Beta-2 microglobulin, with no cytokine stimulus named

mcqs.explanation: The review says AA deposits are composed mainly of serum amyloid A, synthesised by hepatocytes in response to IL-1, IL-6, and TNF.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Amyloid deposits in AA amyloidosis are composed mainly of the serum amyloid A (SAA) protein, an apolipoprotein of high-density lipoproteins that serves as a dynamic acute phase reactant. 5 It is synthesized as a precursor by hepatocytes in response to transcriptional stimuli from various proinflammatory cytokines, such as interleukin (IL)-1, IL-6, and tumor necrosis factor (TNF) alpha.

mcqs.question: What tinctorial finding does the review still call the gold standard for amyloid?

options.A: Congo red avidity and metachromatic birefringence under unidirectional polarised light

mcqs.explanation: Avidity for Congo red and metachromatic birefringence under unidirectional polarised light remain the gold standard.

sourceRefs.excerpt: avidity for Congo red and metachromatic birefringence under unidirectional polarized light remain the gold standard.

mcqs.question: What technique does the review describe for mapping systemic amyloid deposits?

options.A: Radiolabelled serum amyloid P component scintigraphy
options.B: A plain chest radiograph as the only map

mcqs.explanation: The review describes 123-iodine-labelled serum amyloid P component scintigraphy as a safe noninvasive method that identifies anatomical patterns of deposition.

sourceRefs.excerpt: 123 I-labeled serum amyloid P component scintigraphy is a safe and noninvasive technique

mcqs.question: What early clinical finding should raise suspicion of AA amyloidosis in chronic inflammatory disease, and how often may it be present?

options.A: Proteinuria, which may be present in up to 95% of patients and determines prognosis
options.B: A rash in every patient and no renal finding
options.C: Isolated macroglossia as the first sign
options.D: Proteinuria in fewer than 5% of patients

mcqs.explanation: Proteinuria leading to nephrotic syndrome is the earliest and most frequent manifestation in chronic inflammatory conditions. Proteinuria may be present in up to 95% of patients and determines prognosis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Proteinuria may be present in up to 95% of patients and determines prognosis.

mcqs.question: In developed countries, which diseases does the review group as accounting for up to 90% of recent AA amyloidosis?

options.A: Autoimmune diseases such as RA, ankylosing spondylitis, chronic juvenile arthritis, and inflammatory bowel disease, together with hereditary inflammatory diseases
options.C: Acute gout as the only cause
options.D: The review names no inflammatory causes

mcqs.explanation: The review says that in developed countries those autoimmune diseases, including RA and chronic juvenile arthritis, or hereditary inflammatory diseases such as FMF, can account for up to 90% of recent cases. The 90% figure is for that group, not for rheumatoid arthritis alone.

sourceRefs.excerpt: autoimmune diseases such as RA, ankylosing spondylitis, chronic juvenile arthritis, and inflammatory bowel disease, or hereditary inflammatory diseases, such as FMF, TNF receptor-associated periodic syndrome, or Muckle–Wells syndrome, can account for up to 90% of recent cases of amyloidosis.
